items.title: Herb Morand Interview, 1950-03-12
items.q: And we was playing at the Silver Store and Sidney came in. And that's where Sidney had a chance to hear me. So he sat down and he asked me to play different numbers for him.

ctx.x: Around that time, didn't you get an offer from Sidney Boucher to join him in Boston? A few years after that, at least.

Yeah, when Sidney came down here to play the jazz concert at the auditorium with Lewis Armstrong, he had a chance to hear me. He had a chance to hear me. At that time, I was playing with Walter Nelson. He is standing right behind me at the Silver Store at St. Bernard and in that street, I think, or 8 Court. And we was playing there with Walter Nelson, one of the greatest blues guitar players in New Orleans. I am playing with him right now at this time right now. He's standing right over me. Just happened to come…

in Mississippi, Gulfport, Mississippi, Biloxi, a place like that. And I was really doing good. So, I was really sorry that I couldn't make the trip to go up there. But it's one of them things, I wouldn't leave Mama and she's sick to go for it. No, nobody. Yes, I'm sure that was
